explanation: Cropping is a copy loop with an offset: output pixel (col, row) reads source pixel (startX + col, startY + row), so the whole job is choosing a safe starting corner and a safe size. Math.max and Math.min pin the requested x, y, width and height inside the source bounds, which is what keeps getRGB from throwing on an off-image request. Because every pixel is written into a freshly constructed BufferedImage, the caller's image is never touched.
